subject: Structuring 12–24m commitment with credit stacking and usage flexibility
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@neonwave.com>

Cc: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@neonwave.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: commitment structure + credits for 12-24m

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — our team liked the latency profile and the cost tooling. We are sizing a multi-environment deployment and want to explore committing for 12–24 months to simplify forecasting. Two quick asks: can Redwood stack prepaid credits against overages (so credits apply before overage billing), and can we get a staged ramp so we pay less in Q1 as our usage warms up?

We are an early-stage infra startup (~$12M ARR) so the finance team expects straightforward invoicing and a modest term discount. Attaching a simple usage spreadsheet at a later point if helpful.

High level: looking for a ~$120k–200k annual commitment equivalent, with a 12–24 month option and an option to add burst credits for unpredictable spikes.

Would love to get a proposal that shows (a) contract term options (12 vs 24), (b) discount tiers by commit size, and (c) a ramp schedule with credit vesting.

Thanks,

Liam O'Neill
Head of Platform, NeonWave Labs

Subject: Re: Inquiry: commitment structure + credits for 12-24m

Hi Liam — thanks for the detail and context. I ran this past Sales Ops and CS and sketched a pragmatic approach that balances early-stage cash constraints with predictable economics for Redwood. High level options below; I attached a first-pass pricing model and a draft SOW for language.

Option A — 12-month starter
- Commitment: $120k annual prepay (billed upfront or net-30 invoice)
- Discount: 15% off list pro-rata token rates
- Ramp: 0–3 months: 30% of credits inactive (vest monthly); months 4–12: remaining credits unlock linearly
- Overages: Credits are consumed first, then overage billing at post-discount rates

Option B — 24-month growth (recommended if you want better unit economics)
- Commitment: $200k/year (billed annually or semi-annually)
- Discount: 22% off list
- Ramp: First 6 months: 40% of year-1 credits held in reserve and released on milestone (PO + production verification); year-2 credits fully available
- Early termination: pro-rated refund on unused credits less a 10% admin fee

Credit stacking behavior
- Prepaid credits apply before any per-use invoice; credits can be earmarked for a project tag (e.g., production vs staging) but we can allow pooled credits if you prefer simpler accounting.

I left room in the model for invoice cadence (upfront vs annual vs quarterly) — see pricing-model-NW.csv and SOW-draft-NW_v2.docx attached. If you want a PO to match a specific invoicing cadence, tell me the timing and I’ll confirm with Finance.

Next steps I propose: review the two options, tell me preferred term (12 vs 24) and invoicing cadence, and we’ll produce a short MAP (mutual action plan) that ties milestones to credit vesting.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Thanks Karthik — that is very helpful. A couple clarifying questions before we loop legal:

1) For Option B, can NeonWave apply year-1 unused credits to year-2 consumption if we exceed year-2 usage (i.e., negative carry-forward)?
2) Is the 22% discount layered on top of any token-level volume discounts, or is that the effective cap?
3) Can the ramp milestone be tied to "10k MAUs verified" or do you need infra-specific checks (health endpoints)? Our product team prefers usage-based milestones.

We prefer annual billing but would like a 30–45 day PO window aligned to our finance cadence. Also interested in a small burst pool (one-off credits) that we can purchase as needed at a pre-agreed top-up price.

Sophie and I are available for a 30-min call Thursday to finalize approach.

—Liam

Hey all — quick legal/ops notes from Sales Ops:

- Carry-forward: We typically do not do negative carry-forward (i.e., applying unused year-1 credits forward to year-2 beyond the committed amount). We can, however, allow positive carry-forward from year-2 back into year-1 for reconciliation if both sides agree (one-time true-up).
- Discount stacking: the stated % is the effective discount on our published rates; we do not stack separate volume tier discounts on top of an agreed commitment discount unless explicitly called out in the SOW. We can add a graduated pricing table if you expect step-changes in usage that should trigger additional tiered pricing.
- Milestone gating: metrics like "10k MAUs" are fine as a vesting trigger — we only need a simple acceptance test: a telemetry spike report + product owner sign-off.
- Invoice cadence: annual prepay invoiced upfront is standard; we can accept net-30 for startups with credit references but that requires an internal Finance approval (reasonable for $120k–200k).

I updated the SOW with suggested language on credit vesting and termination liability. See SOW-draft-NW_v2.docx.

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Updated term sheet & MAP for NeonWave (v1)

Liam / Sophie — attached is an updated one-pager that captures the agreed approach and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP):

- Term: 24 months preferred by NeonWave (we show both 12/24 for flexibility)
- Commit: $200k/year (annual invoice, net-30 by agreement)
- Discount: flat 22% applied to Redwood list rates for committed consumption
- Credit vesting: 40% of year-1 credits held in escrow, released on two milestones: (1) PO + production verification (up to 20%) and (2) 10k MAUs acceptance test (remaining 20%)
- Carry behavior: unused credits from year-1 are reconciled at year-2 start; any overage in year-2 is billed at the post-discount rate (no negative roll-forward)
- Burst pool: $25k on-demand top-up at a fixed top-up price (pre-agreed)

MAP next steps (proposed):
1) NeonWave to confirm term and invoice cadence (due Oct 13)
2) Redwood to send final SOW and contract redline (due Oct 14)
3) NeonWave legal to return PO and requested invoicing terms (due Oct 20)

If these dates work I will push the SOW to Legal and draft the contract with the specified vesting language.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this for Q4.

Karthik Iyer
